# Project plan {#sec-timeline}

## Start-up phase

Start-up is largely complete because the project is already in motion. The code is public on GitHub with issue tracking open, releases are documented in `NEWS.md`, and milestone updates will be posted to blogs. Licensing is described under Other aspects.

- **Collaboration platform:** existing public GitHub repository (`github.com/paytonyau/OptSurvCutR`), with issue tracking already open. No new platform setup required.
- **License:** GPL-3 for the package (already set on CRAN); CC-BY for documentation and vignettes.
- **Reporting framework:** a `NEWS.md` entry per release (existing practice, already followed through v0.11.1); milestone-linked updates posted to the R Consortium blog (see Other aspects, below) rather than a separate private reporting channel.

## Technical delivery

**Milestone 1 - Simulation study (target: month 1-3; not yet started).** Data simulated under known one-cut and two-cut ground truths, across multiple sample sizes and event rates, testing whether the package's stability tiers predict out-of-sample recovery of the true threshold. Deliverable: public simulation code, results, and a written report.

**Milestone 2 - Preprint update and journal submission (target: month 3-5).** Update the bioRxiv preprint to incorporate Milestone 1's results and any `rOpenSci` review outcomes finalised by this point; submit the manuscript to *BMC Bioinformatics*. Deliverable: updated preprint and submitted manuscript.

**Milestone 3 - Clinician-runnable script and `rOpenSci` completion (target: month 3-6, ongoing throughout).** A single R script (or Quarto document) that takes a clinician's own dataset (one row per patient: predictor, follow-up time, event status, optional covariates), runs the package's three-step pipeline, and produces a plain-language summary and standard plots, configured by naming a handful of columns. It is delivered alongside the remaining `rOpenSci` recommendations. Deliverable: script, short usage guide and worked PBC example; `rOpenSci` acceptance or a clear remaining action list.

## Other aspects

Open-source under GPL-3 (package) and CC-BY (documentation and vignettes). Hosted on the existing public GitHub repository, with issue tracking open to outside contributions. Publicity plan:

- **Announcement post** for this grant, on acceptance
- **Delivery blog posts** at months 3, 5 and 6, so progress is visible incrementally
- **Social media** at each milestone
- **Talks:** we have given talks at FOSDEM 2026 and R!sk 2026, and have submitted an abstract to the 3rd International Online Conference on Genes (2 to 4 December 2026, online); acceptance is pending.
- **ISC meetings:** available to attend or give a progress update if invited.
- **User feedback:** when we learn of published or public use of the package (citations, preprints, GitHub issues), we will ask the authors for brief feedback and, with their permission, list the use case on a public users page. This feedback will test the assumption behind Milestone 3 that users want a simpler entry point.

## Budget & funding plan

| Milestone | Work | Requested amount |
|---|---|---|
| 1 - Simulation study | Design, run and report | $700 |
| 2 - Preprint and submission | Update preprint, submit to *BMC Bioinformatics* | $700 |
| 3 - Script and rOpenSci | Build script; respond to review | $700 |

At 2 to 3 hours a week each over six months, that is about 65 hours each, or about 130 hours in total, costed at about $16 per hour. No other costs are included.
